question: A man walks a square plot of area 121 m². If he walks once around its boundary, how far does he walk?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Side of the square = √Area = √121 = 11 m.

Distance walked in one round = Perimeter of the square.

Perimeter = 4 × Side = 4 × 11 = 44 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 44 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Area of the square plot = 121 m²

**Formula Used:**

Area of a square = (Side)²

Perimeter of a square = 4 × Side

 Area = 121 m2 Side = 11 m 11 m 11 m 11 m 11 m Distance Walked = Perimeter 

**Calculations:**

⇒ (Side)² = 121

⇒ Side = √121

⇒ Side = 11 m

The man walks once around the boundary, which is exactly equal to the perimeter of the square plot.

⇒ Perimeter = 4 × Side

⇒ Perimeter = 4 × 11

⇒ Perimeter = 44 m

**∴ The correct answer is 44 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of a Square

The region enclosed by the boundaries of a square is its area. It is given by the square of its side: Area = a², or by using the diagonal length (d): Area = d² ÷ 2.

Perimeter of a Square

The total length of the outer boundary of the square is its perimeter. It is calculated by adding all four equal sides together: Perimeter = 4a.

Diagonal of a Square

The straight line segment connecting two opposite corners of a square. Its length is calculated using the Pythagorean theorem as: Diagonal = a√2.
